summary: Backend-only production tests for NOVA 4 Rule 0 fix on Railway. All 5 tests pass: Philadelphia coerced to Ultra-Processed score 3, Babybel Light 9/Processed (no regression), Peter's Yard 8/Processed, Welch's 1/Ultra-Processed, and 1 rescan call confirmed determinism (score=3, category=ultra-processed, upf_score=unknown — proving Rule 0 masked the contradictory low UPF%).
critical_code_review_comments: Rule 0 correctly positioned at line 883 BEFORE Rule 1/2 chain (line 892+); upf_pct is parsed at line 862 before Rule 0 reads it — control flow correct.
/app/server.py is byte-identical to /app/backend/server.py (diff -q returned no output).
Rule 0 uses both off_nova_group==4 (authoritative OpenFoodFacts data) AND ai_flagged_nova4 (marker-additive detection) as OR conditions — robust dual signal.
server.py is 3766 lines — consider splitting into modules (routes, scoring, off_client, cache) for maintainability.
Rule 9 UPF safety net (line 911) correctly gated on 'ultra' not in category, so it cannot override the Rule 0 coercion.
seed_data_creation: none — used existing production cache entries
context_for_next_testing_agent: Rule 0 (NOVA 4 coercion) is verified working on prod. Rescan endpoint costs OpenAI money — limit to 1 call per test run. Test file /app/backend/tests/test_production_nova4_fix.py is reusable regression suite.
rca of the issue: Original bug: AI returned processing_category='Processed' AND flagged guar gum as NOVA 4 in harmful_ingredients — self-contradictory. Rule 2 (min score 3) only fired on category='ultra-processed' string, so contradictory AI output escaped the cap. Fix (Rule 0) forces category to 'Ultra-Processed' when either OFF nova_group==4 or AI flags any NOVA 4 additive, THEN Rule 2 applies the score cap. Verified: rescan of Philadelphia yields score=3, category=ultra-processed, upf_score='unknown' (masked because AI's low UPF% contradicted the NOVA 4 classification).
